entries.title: Stranglethorn Vale
body: A vast tropical jungle filling the southern end of the Eastern Kingdoms, from Duskwood to the Cape of Stranglethorn. Tigers, panthers, raptors and gorillas hunt under its canopy, and crocolisks and naga crowd its rivers and coasts.

This was once the heart of the Gurubashi troll empire, and its ruins are everywhere, held now by the Bloodscalp and Skullsplitter tribes who war with each other and everyone else. Over the trolls lie newer quarrels: the goblin port of Booty Bay, the Venture Company's mines, the Horde's camp at Grom'gol, Alliance rebels, ogres, pirates, and big game hunters who have come for the trophies.

entries.title: Booty Bay
body: A goblin port built into the cliffs of a sheltered bay at the southern tip of the jungle, entered through the open jaws of a giant shark skull. It belongs to the Steamwheedle Cartel and is ruled by Baron Revilgaz, the most notorious pirate on the South Seas, whose Blackwater Raiders run the town.

Anyone may trade here and nobody asks many questions. Krazek keeps an ear out for rumours and snorts dream dust; Kebok counts the costs of the trolls killing his agents; Drizzlik makes boots for the Tinkers' Union; Sea Wolf MacKinley collects gambling debts, from the living and the cursed alike.
sources: quest 599 reward text (Booty Bay will always be run by the Blackwater Raiders)

entries.title: Grom'gol Base Camp
body: The Warchief's base camp on the western coast of Stranglethorn, whose zeppelins link the jungle to Orgrimmar and the Undercity. Its mission is to keep a safe chain of supply to Stonard, and Commander Aggro'gosh tolerates no slackers.

The Horde did not come to make war on the jungle's tribes, but the raptors and the ogres of the Mizjah Ruins have made it necessary. Darkspear trolls sent from Orgrimmar camp here too, looking for their chief's lost son, and Far Seer Mok'thardin works rituals with the jungle's magic, knowing that Hellscream's eyes are on even this remote corner of the world.

entries.title: Nesingwary's Expedition
body: A big game hunters' camp in northern Stranglethorn, upriver of Lake Nazferiti. It is led by Hemet Nesingwary Jr., son of the famous war hero and hunter, with his companions Ajeck Rouack and Sir S. J. Erlgadin and his proofreader Barnil Stonepot.

They are here for one thing: trophies. Tigers, panthers and raptors are hunted in rising order of difficulty, up to the legendary beasts Sin'Dall, Bhag'thera and Tethis, and finally King Bangalash, the great white tiger. Nesingwary is also writing a novel about it all, The Green Hills of Stranglethorn, whose pages a gust of wind scattered across the jungle.

entries.title: The Rebel Camp
body: A small Alliance camp in the north-west of the jungle, near the road from Duskwood. Its soldiers were once the fiercely loyal men of Colonel Kurzen; when Kurzen fell into corruption, they rebelled, and now they are hunted by him.

Lieutenant Doren leads them. They are outnumbered ten to one and have to use the colonel's own covert tactics against him. Even inside the camp they are not safe: a spy named Private Merle was found among them, and Brother Nimetz searches the troll ruins for whatever turned Kurzen evil.

entries.title: Kurzen's Compound
body: The fortified camp of Colonel Kurzen in northern Stranglethorn, east of the Rebel Camp. Kurzen was sent to the jungle as a great and noble man, and became something else entirely. His jungle fighters, medicine men, headshrinkers and commandos are skilled, loyal and cruel.
Deep at the back of the compound is a cave called the Stockpile, where the colonel commands his men. His logistics officer, Bookie Herod, kept his records in the camp's only two-storey house.

entries.title: The Mosh'Ogg Mound
body: An ogre mound in the eastern mountains of Stranglethorn. The Mosh'Ogg ogres who live there gamble with any pirate fool enough to sit down with them.

Their ogre mage, Mai'Zoth, holds the Mind's Eye, a jewel from the heart of the jungle with the power to bend minds. The Darkspears knew him from their days in Stranglethorn, and Brother Nimetz believes it was Mai'Zoth who corrupted Colonel Kurzen.

entries.title: The Bloodscalp Ruins
body: Ruins in the north-west of the jungle, at Bal'lal and Tkashi and around Zul'Kunda, held by the Bloodscalp trolls. Their headhunters carry shrunken heads, and their chief, Gan'zulah, and his witch doctor Nezzliok are old enemies of the Darkspear tribe.

The Bloodscalps use tactics much like those of the Amani of the north, but their magic has gone somewhere strange. A totem taken from one of their shamans named its true patron: Naias, a water elemental living on an island off the coast.

entries.title: The Skullsplitter Ruins
body: Ruined troll cities in the south-east of the jungle, at Balia'mah, Ziata'jai and Zul'Mamwe, held by the Skullsplitter tribe. They war with the Bloodscalps, and the Darkspears remain bound to their feud with them even though the Darkspears left the jungle long ago.
Their chief is Ana'thek the Cruel. Booty Bay's merchants have a less noble interest in them: Skullsplitter tusks are close enough to tiger fangs to be passed off as the real thing in the South Seas.

entries.title: Zul'Gurub
body: The ancient capital of the Gurubashi Empire in north-eastern Stranglethorn. Before the Darkspears left with Thrall, it was their custom to give children to the Gurubashi of Zul'Gurub.

Now Hakkar the Soulflayer, the Blood God, has been brought back into the world there. Trolls of the Zandalar tribe have come from their distant islands to Yojamba Isle off the northern coast, led by Molthor, the Hand of Rastakhan, and recruit heroes to enter the city and banish the god.

entries.title: The Gurubashi Arena
body: A great stone arena in the middle of the jungle, built by the Gurubashi trolls for their games. Pirates run it now.
Short John Mithril drops a chest of treasure into the ring every few hours, and everyone inside fights for it. Those who spill enough blood on the arena floor earn the title of Grandmaster.

entries.title: The Ruins of Aboraz and Jubuwal
body: Ruins north-east of Booty Bay, along the Crystal Shore, where the witch doctor Zanzil the Outcast lives with his followers: zombies, skeletons, and trolls and naga whose wills he has taken.

Zanzil was exiled from his tribe because its leaders feared him. He bends minds with a mixture of jungle plants that suppresses the will and strengthens the body. Booty Bay's goblins buy it to brew Fool's Stout.

entries.title: The Vile Reef
body: A sunken troll city off the Savage Coast in the north-west, drowned long ago when the earth shuddered. Murlocs live in its ruins and attack anyone who comes near.

Among the ruins lies an old tablet telling the tale of Gri'lek, a hero of troll legend. Not far away, on a haunted island, a goblin mage named Gazban once found the Stone of the Tides, a troll relic that curses its bearer to fade in and out of existence.

entries.title: Jaguero Isle
body: An island in the South Seas off the Cape of Stranglethorn, whose apes are ruled by the great Skymane King Mukla.

Mukla holds a captive there, chained by the beasts of the island: Princess Poobah, who threw a message in a bottle into the sea in the hope that someone on the large sailing ships she could see would read it.

entries.title: Janeiro's Point
body: A small island off the western coast of the jungle. The sea giant Mok'rash stands there beside a statue and bellows across the water for Captain Hecklebury Smotts to come out and play.

Smotts was a successful captain on the Ratchet run until three sea giants, Gorlash, Negolash and Mok'rash, smashed his ship and killed his crew. He bought another, named it Smotts' Revenge, and lost that one too. He now lives for revenge in Booty Bay, and a lifeboat on the beach marks where the giants left him.

entries.title: The Wild Shore
body: The southern beaches below Booty Bay, where the Bloodsail Buccaneers have set up their command post. Their fleet lies anchored just off the cape, under Fleet Master Firallon aboard the Crimson Veil.
The Bloodsail are the Blackwater Raiders' rivals, and they mean to take Booty Bay. A map found in a skiff north of town showed exactly where their men were to hide and wait for the signal to attack.

entries.title: Yenniku
body: The youngest son of Vol'jin's predecessor as chief of the Darkspears. It was the custom of his people to give a child to the Gurubashi of Zul'Gurub, and Yenniku was given; when the Darkspears left Stranglethorn with Thrall, he was lost to them.

The Horde sent Nimboya from Orgrimmar to find him. The heads of the Bloodscalp chief and his witch doctor, made to speak, revealed that Zanzil the Outcast had taken him, body and soul. Only the Mind's Eye, reshaped into a soul gem, could free him from the witch doctor's will.

entries.title: Colonel Kurzen
body: A brilliant tactician and once a great, noble man, the commander of an Alliance force sent into Stranglethorn. Something in the jungle changed him, and his own soldiers rebelled.

Brother Nimetz searched troll tablets and Skullsplitter fetishes for the cause and found it in Mai'Zoth, the ogre mage whose Mind's Eye can corrupt the minds of others. Nimetz feared that as long as Mai'Zoth lived, another Kurzen could rise.

entries.title: The Gurubashi Empire
body: Thousands of years ago the Gurubashi trolls ruled this jungle and the lands around it. When their empire began to fail, they turned to Hakkar the Soulflayer, and the Blood God demanded sacrifices without end. The tribes rose against his priests, the Atal'ai, and drove them out.

The empire did not survive. Its cities were broken, some sunk by earthquakes, and the jungle is now full of their ruins, held by the tribes that came after: the Bloodscalps, the Skullsplitters, and once the Darkspears. Their legends survive on tablets in the ruins, telling of heroes like Gri'lek.
sources: pre-Cataclysm lore: the Gurubashi Empire and Hakkar

entries.title: The Blackwater Raiders and the Bloodsail
body: Booty Bay is run by the Blackwater Raiders, whose captain is Baron Revilgaz himself and whose fleet master is the old sea dog Seahorn. Their rivals, the Bloodsail Buccaneers, have long wanted the bay for themselves.

The Bloodsail planned an attack from the Wild Shore. The Raiders learned the plan and struck first, at their captains and their fleet master. The Bloodsail, for their part, offer a place to anyone who is no friend of Booty Bay, and promise that with Revilgaz and Seahorn dead, they could sail where they liked and take what they wanted.
